subject: Post-call: GDPR / DPA / SCC selection (Medoria)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Kostova <elena@medoria.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:04:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: GDPR / DPA / SCC selection (Medoria)

Hi Elena — great to meet today. Thanks for the time and the walk-through of Medoria's integration and data flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on GDPR/DPA/SCC items before legal review: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood is currently SOC 2 Type I (completed) and targeting Type II audit completion in Q3 2026. We can share the Type I report and our SOC roadmap; we'll include the SOC timeline in the DPA as an appendix.

2) GDPR roles: From our discussion it sounds like Medoria will be the Controller and Redwood will act as Processor for customer data originating from Medoria's users. Please confirm this mapping — if there are any parts where Redwood is acting as an independent Controller (e.g., aggregate analytics outside customer accounts) call that out.

3) SCCs / Module selection: Per typical controller→processor transfers, our standard approach is to use the Controller-to-Processor SCC module (we've attached a short guidance sheet: SCC-Module-Selection-Medoria.xlsx). If you confirm, we'll prepare the DPA using that module.

4) HIPAA / PHI: You mentioned potential PHI flows via the telemetry pipeline. If Medoria expects PHI processing by Redwood, we'll need to include a BAA addendum. Otherwise the standard DPA (with SCCs) should be sufficient.

5) Next steps: 
- Please confirm: a) Medoria is Controller, b) any PHI will be processed, and c) whether you prefer our standard DPA or your procurement DPA.
- I'll send our draft DPA and suggested SCC module selection to your legal.
- If you want to complete a vendor security questionnaire, we can send a short intake link — or if you prefer, share your PDF and we'll fill.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_Draft_20260224.pdf and SCC-Module-Selection-Medoria.xlsx for your review.

If you confirm the Controller→Processor mapping and no PHI, we can aim to have a signed DPA within 1-2 weeks (legal permitting).

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the ping and the thread — good notes. Quick legal: 

- SCC module: confirmed. We'll use the Controller-to-Processor (Controller→Processor) SCC module in the DPA; that's the appropriate module for the transfer path described.

- HIPAA / BAA: because Medoria indicated PHI will be processed, we should include BAA language. Our standard approach: add HIPAA-specific clauses as an exhibit to the DPA (so we don't need a standalone contract for the initial review). If Medoria prefers a separate BAA, we can prepare that as an addendum.

- SOC2 evidence: the Type I report + a short SOC roadmap is usually sufficient to move forward for procurement. If they insist on Type II evidence before POC, we can discuss; for now, provide Type I and SOC roadmap appendix.

I've reviewed the draft and attached a redline (DPA_Redline_Dev_20260225.pdf) with: 
- Minor language clarifications on data deletion timing.
- Added Exhibit B with HIPAA/BAA language and a placeholder for the SCC module selection table.

Next steps (recommended):
1) Marissa: share the redlined DPA and the short vendor intake link with Elena/Oliver.
2) Procurement: Medoria to confirm they accept DPA with exhibit for BAA or request a standalone BAA.
3) Legal (both sides): aim to clear DPA + BAA exhibit and sign within 7-10 business days if no major commercial changes.

I'll be on call if they want to do a legal sync — happy to jump into a short call.

Best,
